newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Govt agrees review Lisnave restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Govt agrees review Lisnave restructuring.

text.p: The Portuguese government said it had agreed to renegotiate a restructuring plan for ailing ship repairer Lisnave-Estaleiros Navais de Lisboa.

A statement published in the official daily Diario da Republica said the Finance Ministry would study how a Lisnave bond loan of six billion escudos, which matures on November 15, could be restructured.

The government, which holds a 15 percent stake in Lisnave, said such a solution was necessary "to safeguard the image and credibility of the company, particularly in the financial markets and to avoid non-payment which would invalidate the overall restructuring plan."

The statement said Portugal's finance and economy ministers would negotiate with Lisnave shareholders the Mello group over Lisnave's continued restructuring, taking into account the requirements for approval by the European Commission.
It said concrete restructuring measures should come into effect by the end of the year.
The Mello group recently signed an accord with Germany's Thyssen Werften aimed at making Lisnave's yards profitable.
Lisnave shares closed up 12 escudos at 435 on volume of 150,350.
